newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Nationwide '96 pretax profit up 10.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Irish Nationwide '96 pretax profit up 10.6 pct.

text.p: The Irish Nationwide Building Society said on Tuesday that 1996 pretax profits rose 10.6 percent to 24.365 million Irish pounds.

The building society said in a results statement that assets grew 14 percent to a record high of 1.09 billion Irish pounds and mortgage advances rose to 240.10 million pounds from 154.539 the previous year.
This represented an increase of 15 percent, also a new record the society, it said.

Managing Director Michael Fingleton said that in 1997 the society anticipates another year of strong demand for mortgages and is expecting house prices to increase by 15 percent. "The continuing low level of interest rates has been the principal factor fuelling demand and we expect the present level of interest rates to be maintained for the remainder of the year," he said.
He said that despite strong growth the society managed to reduce its cost/income ratio to 32 percent from 34 percent and said cost control gave it an advantage over competitors.
